title: Kintampo begins clinical trial of Lassa Fever vaccine - Modern Ghana

analysis.time: Home Radio TV Videos Movies Advertise Ghana Contact Login NEWS SPORTS BUSINESS POLITICS OPINIONS HEALTH AFRICA WORLD ENTERTAINMENT LIFESTYLE SCIENCE TECHNOLOGY NOLLYWOOD MEDIA MEMBERS Archive Health News Family/Parenting Home/Food Health/Fitness Spirituality OnAIR Search Kintampo begins clinical trial of Lassa Fever vaccine By Grace Acheampong, ISD || contributor Health MON, 19 OCT 2026 The Kintampo Health Research Centre (KHRC) has begun testing a vaccine candidate against Lassa fever, marking a new step in efforts to develop protection against the disease in Ghana and other West African countries.
analysis.location_and_population: Kintampo North Municipality and Kintampo South District, Ghana.
analysis.event: Kintampo Health Research Centre (KHRC) begins a Phase 1b clinical trial of a ChAdOx1 LassaJ vaccine candidate to assess its safety and immune response in healthy adults.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The trial involves 51 participants and is expected to provide evidence on the vaccine’s safety and immune response, which could inform subsequent stages of its development. No specific case or death counts are reported.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The trial is sponsored by the University of Oxford and funded by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI). The vaccine uses the same technology platform as the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. The study protocol has undergone regulatory reviews in Ghana and the UK.

analysis.brief_en: Kintampo Health Research Centre in Ghana has begun a Phase 1b clinical trial of a ChAdOx1 LassaJ vaccine candidate to assess its safety and immune response in 51 healthy adults aged 18 to 55 from Kintampo North Municipality and Kintampo South District. The trial, sponsored by the University of Oxford and funded by CEPI, aims to provide evidence that could inform subsequent stages of vaccine development. No specific case or death counts are reported.
analysis.summary_en: Kintampo Health Research Centre in Ghana has begun a Phase 1b clinical trial of a ChAdOx1 LassaJ vaccine candidate to assess its safety and immune response in 51 healthy adults aged 18 to 55 from Kintampo North Municipality and Kintampo South District. The trial, sponsored by the University of Oxford and funded by CEPI, aims to provide evidence that could inform subsequent stages of vaccine development. No specific case or death counts are reported.

title: Malaria may mask early detection of Ebola, Lassa fever — Virologist - Realnews Magazine

analysis.location_and_population: Nigeria, Abuja; tropical countries where malaria is endemic.
analysis.event: A virologist, Dr Solomon Chollom, warned that the persistent burden of malaria in tropical countries may complicate the early detection of infectious diseases like Ebola and Lassa fever. This is a suspected issue based on expert opinion.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The diagnostic challenge could lead to delayed treatment and public health measures, increasing the risk of spread for diseases such as Lassa fever and Ebola. No specific case or death counts were reported.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The expert called for strengthening disease surveillance and diagnostic procedures, as well as reviewing malaria control strategies. The situation remains under investigation and requires further action.

analysis.brief_en: A virologist, Dr Solomon Chollom, has raised concerns that the persistent presence of malaria in tropical countries may hinder the early detection of other infectious diseases, such as Ebola and Lassa fever. In an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Abuja on Thursday, October 22, 2026, Chollom highlighted that the early symptoms of malaria can be similar to those of other diseases, leading to misdiagnosis and delaying appropriate treatment and public health responses. He emphasized the need for improved diagnostic services and surveillance systems to ensure that healthcare workers consider other potential causes of fever, especially in regions where multiple infectious diseases coexist. Chollom also urged governments to evaluate the effectiveness of malaria control policies and integrate them with broader efforts to prepare for emerging infections. The situation remains under investigation, with the expert calling for a comprehensive review of interventions to address gaps and enhance preparedness for future outbreaks.

title: Anambra govt confirms Lassa fever case, activates emergency response - Businessday NG

analysis.time: The Anambra State Government confirmed the case on Monday, October 19, 2026. The event date is October 19, 2026, and the response was activated on the same day.
analysis.location_and_population: The case was linked to Omasi community in Ayamelum Local Government Area, Anambra State, Nigeria. The affected population includes residents of Omasi, other communities in Ayamelum, and the wider state.
analysis.event: The Anambra State Government confirmed a case of Lassa fever, which is a viral illness transmitted through contact with infected rodents. The confirmation was made by Afam Obidike, the Commissioner for Health, during an emergency stakeholders’ meeting.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The confirmed case has triggered an emergency response to prevent further transmission. The government is monitoring potential contacts and implementing measures to strengthen disease surveillance and public awareness. The risk of further transmission is explicitly stated as a concern.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The government has activated the Incident Management System (IMS) to manage the public health emergency. Health partners such as WHO and MSF were present at the meeting. The response includes follow-up activities at the affected household, identification of contacts, and preventive measures to reduce exposure to rodents.

analysis.brief_en: The Anambra State Government confirmed a case of Lassa fever linked to Omasi community in Ayamelum Local Government Area on Monday, October 19, 2026. The case was disclosed by Afam Obidike, the Commissioner for Health, during an emergency stakeholders’ meeting at the Ministry of Health headquarters in Awka. The patient is receiving treatment at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Abakaliki (FETHA) in Ebonyi State. The government has activated an emergency response, including the Incident Management System (IMS), to prevent further transmission. Measures involve monitoring potential contacts, strengthening disease surveillance, and raising public awareness. Health partners such as the World Health Organisation (WHO) and Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) were present at the meeting. Residents are urged to remain vigilant, avoid self-medication, and report suspected cases promptly. Preventive actions include keeping food covered, using rodent-proof containers, and maintaining clean surroundings to reduce exposure to rodents. The response aims to contain the outbreak and minimize the risk of further spread.

The case was disclosed by Afam Obidike, the Commissioner for Health, during an emergency stakeholders’ meeting at the Ministry of Health headquarters in Awka. The patient is receiving treatment at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Abakaliki (FETHA) in Ebonyi State. The government has activated an emergency response, including the Incident Management System (IMS), to prevent further transmission. Measures involve monitoring potential contacts, strengthening disease surveillance, and raising public awareness. Health partners such as the World Health Organisation (WHO) and Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) were present at the meeting. Residents are urged to remain vigilant, avoid self-medication, and report suspected cases promptly. title: MerTK links dexamethasone to weakened antiviral immunity in chronic LCMV infection - Bioengineer.org

analysis.time: The study was published on October 21, 2026. The experiment involved mice infected with LCMV and treated with dexamethasone starting on days 2, 4, and 6 after infection.
analysis.location_and_population: The study was conducted on mice aged 7–10 weeks, including both male and female individuals, infected with the LCMV Docile strain.
analysis.event: A study published by Bioengineer.org on October 21, 2026, found that dexamethasone suppressed antiviral CD8+ T-cell immunity and increased LCMV replication in chronically infected wild-type mice. The findings were based on experiments comparing wild-type Mertk+/+ mice with MerTK-deficient Mertk–/– littermate controls.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Dexamethasone caused a pronounced loss of total and virus-specific CD8+ T cells in wild-type mice, with a decline in blood, spleen, and liver. The percentage of these cells decreased, and the absolute splenic CD8+ T-cell count was substantially reduced. MerTK-deficient mice retained higher CD8+ T-cell levels and were resistant to the steroid-induced decline. The study also noted that dexamethasone altered the differentiation state of CD8+ T cells, reducing markers like KLRG1, CD44, and CD127, while increasing CD62L. These changes were associated with worse infection outcomes and increased viral dissemination.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study identified MerTK as a central mediator of steroid-associated suppression of antiviral immunity in this mouse model. However, it did not directly test the causal links among MerTK signaling, IL-10, PD-1, and T-cell dysfunction. The results establish a change in the measured cellular state rather than a complete loss of killing capacity.

analysis.brief_en: A study published on October 21, 2026, by Bioengineer.org investigated the effects of dexamethasone on antiviral immunity in mice chronically infected with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV). The research found that dexamethasone suppressed CD8+ T-cell immunity and increased LCMV replication in wild-type mice, while MerTK-deficient mice showed resistance to these effects. The study used male and female mice aged 7–10 weeks infected with the LCMV Docile strain and treated with dexamethasone or phosphate-buffered saline every 48 hours. Immune responses were assessed on day 8 after infection, with findings indicating that MerTK plays a key role in the steroid-induced suppression of antiviral immunity. However, the study did not directly test the causal relationships between MerTK signaling, IL-10, PD-1, and T-cell dysfunction. It also noted that dexamethasone altered the differentiation state of CD8+ T cells, reducing markers like KLRG1, CD44, and CD127, while increasing CD62L. These changes were linked to worse infection outcomes and increased viral dissemination. The results suggest that MerTK is a central mediator of steroid-associated immune suppression in this experimental setting, but further research is needed to confirm these findings in humans.
